chunks: Muhammad ibn Ja'far al-Razzaz narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Abu al-Khattab al-Zayyat, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Isḥaq ibn Jarir, from Abū 'Abdillāh (peace be upon him), who said:

When I was in al-Hīrah, in the presence of Abū al-'Abbās, I would visit the grave of the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) at night, and he was in the region of al-Najaf, on the side of al-Ghārī al-Nu'mān. So I would pray the night prayer there, and I would depart before dawn.

key_terms.النَّجَف: Al-Najaf, a city in Iraq known for Imam Ali's shrine
key_terms.الْحِيرَة: Al-Hīrah, a historical city in Iraq
key_terms.الْغَرِيُّ النُّعْمَان: Al-Ghārī al-Nu'mān, a specific location or landmark near Najaf

ai.seo_question: Where was the grave of Imam Ali (a.s.) located in al-Hīrah according to this narration?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Kamil al-Ziyarat* provides early geographical evidence for the location of Imam Ali’s (a.s.) shrine, situating it in al-Hīrah near the site of al-Ghārī al-Nu'mān, which later became synonymous with al-Najaf. It highlights the practice of *Salat al-Layl* (night prayer) at the grave, emphasizing the spiritual connection between the living and the Imam during the quiet hours before dawn, a tradition deeply valued in Shia piety.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 11. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far Al-Razzāz narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Hajjāl, from Safwān ibn Mihrān, who said:

I asked Abā ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) about the location of the grave of the Commander of the Believers (a.s.). He described that it was located in the land of the hardened sands. I went to the described location and established prayers there. The following year, I went back to the Imam (a.s.) and informed him that I had gone to the described location and had prayed there. He told me that I had found the correct location. For twenty years thereafter, I used to go to that described location every year and establish prayers next to it.
